pr_title: Disallow manual combo colouring when not on beatmap skin
pr_body:
Closes #8282 

Disallows manual combo colouring (aka "color haxing") when not enabling beatmap skin, this is a behaviour on osu!stable and should be a thing here to avoid selecting combo colours of a different skin to hit objects that are not meant to be coloured in that way.

## Breaking changes
### `IHasComboInformation.ComboIndex` and `IHasComboInformation.ComboIndexBindable` have changed types from `int` to `ComboIndex (struct)`
Now `ComboIndex` provides two indices within its structure, automated index which increments by `1` per new combo, and manual index which increments by `1 + ComboOffset` per new combo, to allow switching between manual combo colouring and automated combo colouring.

(We probably do, but it's a little complicated to keep track of in the way done here; maybe this logic should be somehow encapsulated in legacy beatmap decoding?)

I think this is the best approach FWIW. encapsulating in legacy beatmap decoder isn't clear to me, can you elaborate further?

The loose idea would be to check if the beatmap has a skin at parse time and then expose a `ComboIndex` or something at the legacy beatmap level if it does have a skin (so basically have it in `IHasCombo`, maybe?) and then use it only in skinning. I haven't looked in detail if that's viable or if it'll look good in code, however.

I haven't looked in detail if that's viable or if it'll look good in code, however.

so you're simply saying to move `ComboIndex.WithBeatmapOffset` to `IHasCombo` and set it on parse time, that almost sounds like what this PR does but slightly different and on parse time, which is incorrect because the combo index processing must be inside `BeatmapProcessor` for beatmap editing purposes, unless I'm mistaking?
I have another way that doesn't affect the `IHasComboInformation` interface and introduce weird `ComboIndex` structures like that, going to close this as it's gonna be a complete rewrite.

issue_context.title: Disabling beatmap skins option does not fully disable beatmap's combo colors
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** 
When the option ``Beatmap skins`` is disabled, combo color usage is wrong.

* Expected: Combo colors go to only selected skin's values
* Actual: I think it reverts to a modulo operator, so if your skin has two combo colors, every even numbered color in map skin's will be your skin's second color, every odd one your first.

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:**
lazer side: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6e0_x9AzkRs
expected from stable: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3IZHCLjyXIo

**osu!lazer version:** 
2020.312.0
comments: What happens if `Beatmap skins` is on but no beatmap combo colour is available, same results?
No. Then selected skin's combo colors are used correctly: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n03vo6jni9Y
Weirdly, I can't reproduce with normal skins (one generated by code on test and other downloaded), can you please provide the skin you were reproducing against.

The actual issue here is not related to skin combo colours, but rather, it's about hit object manual combo colour assigning (also known as "color haxing") not being disabled when beatmap skin is disabled, will look into fixing this.

review_comments:
so is this the combo's index in the beatmap? if so, you should also look at `IHasCombo.ComboOffset` as it may be similar to what is provided here.

as it stands, this documentation/class feels very hard to understand.

isn't `IHasCombo.ComboOffset` just the amount of combos to skip from current combo index in the processing? this index doesn't let that in its calculation: `Ordinal = lastObj.Ordinal + 1;` (which just increments by 1 per new combo, or as you said "the combo's index in the beatmap")

If osu!stable provides something much saner / straightforward than this, would be better to let me know I suppose.
